Can Sky ecosystem go to zero?

Noticing that a lot of FUD mixes up USDS, sUSDS and stUSDS.

And Sky is complex.

First, remember that MakerDAO rebranded to Sky. DAI still exists, while USDS is the new shiny stable.

The system is now backed by a mix of crypto collateral, other stables and RWAs ($6.5B backed by $9.5B in collateral).

So what matters for USDS is 1) that there's more collateral for DAI and USDS issued, and 2) if people can redeem.

No issues here.

You can also deposit USDS into savings and receive sUSDS, which earns the Sky Savings Rate. Currently around 3.8%.

The yield comes from interest paid by borrowers, RWAs and strategies run via Spark etc.

But then there's stUSDS. The FUD Zone.

Here your USDS backs loans against $SKY collateral.

I totally get the FUD here.

Founders borrowing against their own token isn't a good look and we still remember the drama with Curve's Egorov borrowing against CRV and getting rekt.

But if you deposited to this strategy, you should've known the risk.

Now there's no liquidity to withdraw and they depend on repayments or new deposits.

Is current 25% APY worth the risk to deposit? I want to see Sky here come up with a strategy to repay the loan first.

Dumping SKY doesn't help.

So Sky announced extra buybacks for 7 days, but buying SKY doesn't repay those loans.

stUSDS holders get rekt first if the loans go bad. That helps protect USDS.

TLDR: USDS isn't backed by stUSDS tokens. And your sUSDS savings aren't deposited into this lending pool.

THE DAILY METALS PULSE | NOVEMBER 19 — CLOSING BELL

#Uranium #Silver #Gold #Copper

The morning recovery failed to bring broad relief. Today’s macro data delivered an uncomfortable combination: weaker factory growth, rising costs and a labour market still giving the Fed room to tighten.

🌎 THE PHILLY FED WARNING
November’s survey showed:
• Activity index: 6.3, down from 20.9
• New orders: −0.4
• Input-price index: 58.2, up from 43.2

One regional survey, but a clear warning: growth can weaken before inflation does.

US jobless claims edged up to 203,000, while continuing claims rose to 1.763 million. Some softening, with layoffs still relatively low.

📉 MINERS — LATEST QUOTES (21:40–21:48 GMT)
☢️ $URA −2.5% | $URNM −3.2%
🥈 $SIL −4.2%
🥇 $GDX −3.8%

🥇 GOLD & SILVER
December gold futures settled 1.5% lower at $3,685.50. Spot silver bid was around $42.80, down 4.8%, at 21:52 GMT.

The strong dollar and expectations of further rate hikes continued to weigh.

🔶 COPPER’S PHYSICAL SQUEEZE
Today’s Reuters analysis highlighted Shanghai’s deliverable copper inventories falling to 27,642 tonnes from a March peak above 433,000.

That is local tightness, not proof of a worldwide shortage. But it shows why falling futures prices alone tell an incomplete supply story.

🌍 SUMMIT: LIMITED CONCRETE RELIEF
Trump, Xi and Putin issued a symbolic peace declaration and pledged to increase fuel supplies. The declaration contained no mention of the wars in Ukraine or Iran.

Oil ended almost unchanged: Brent $91.98, WTI $83.21. Shipping risks continued to offset surplus concerns.

My take: the hardest environment for miners is weakening demand alongside stubborn costs and expensive capital. Today’s data reinforced that risk.

I remain bullish on the long-term supply picture. The next convincing recovery needs improving conditions for the businesses behind the tickers.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the daily metals pulse.

I haven't finished the whole podcast (currently listening).

But, my initial thought is that the cost of capital angle is not convincing. If the rise in rents was a function of higher cost of capital, then you would see availability creeping up too (our data). But, all GPUs have had low availability this year and B200s in particular have remained largely unavailable on the spot market (hard to see it but the red line on bottom clip has been pinned to 0% availability for months). We see similar dynamics in our foreign data fwiw.

These availability stats point to demand pushing up rents (i.e. if cost of capital was driving up rents, then we should theoretically see availability soften as the market searches for a new equilibrium and kills marginal demand).

Like I said, though, I haven't finished listening and will keep an open mind.

India is the only place I've felt genuine 'culture shock'. I spent a good few months there when I was younger, with little money, and this was my experience

The first word I think of, when I think of India is overwhelming. In almost every sense:

- The diversity and flavour of the food
- The celebration and visibility of religion and spirituality
- The importance of, and passion for, cricket
- The density of people, noise and traffic
- The scale and proximity of inequality
- The intensity of social interaction, from negotiating everything to the directness of personal questions
- The warm and welcoming nature of the people and their desire to share their culture, both nationally and locally
- The chaotic nature of everyday life, where everything feels co-ordinated in its own disorganisation

Overall, I think India is best understood through its contradictions, both in individual places and across states. One of the biggest of these is how incredibly warm people are individually, and yet how impersonal things can feel in the aggregate, where bureaucratic systems are a nightmare and corruption is commonplace

I remember waiting for a bus and asking a guy at the bus stop when it would arrive. 'Soon, don't worry' A couple of hours passed, so I asked again. 'Soon, my friend' Eventually it got dark, and I asked him one final time. 'Ah, it comes tomorrow. Let's go eat something, macha?'

It's that sort of thing that takes a while to adjust to. Indians seem to have an insanely high tolerance for chaos, and you've got to learn to rely on adjust karna. The idea that you will simply accommodate delays and changes as they happen

It's the type of place you're so happy you've been to, but have a sense of relief when you leave

I imagine that as a tourist with money, you'll experience many of the same things but remain more insulated from them, becoming more of an observer. If you go, go see the beauty of the country but also try to talk to people and experience some of everyday life. The people and communities is what makes India so distinctive

One day I'll probably go back and see it more from this POV. For now it remains a country I have a lot of love for, even if that love is complicated

I can finally share what I’ve been working on at @Microsoft. I lead Today, the product you saw all over the Ignite conference this week.

Today is a new form factor for work. It’s not a chat box it’s a Feed. While you sleep, an AI agent works in the background on your email, your calendar, Teams and your documents. In the morning, the work is already prepared: replies drafted, conflicts spotted, the messages that matter pulled to the top, the documents waiting for your review.

You don’t have to prompt it. There’s nothing to configure. You open Today, check what it did, and in a few taps you send, accept or mark as done. Most of us start the day by digging through everything that came in overnight. With Today, you start by finishing work your agent did.

We think this is what AI at work should feel like: proactive, quiet and useful, without you having to ask.

Today lives in your existing apps starting with Outlook and Copilot meeting customers in the app they use the most.

I had so much fun building it with an incredible team: @JesseProvo, @donovanso, @telmen, @justinchando, Chris Parnin, Gideon Ojo, Alex Trzyna, Christopher Miller, Diana Slaba, Kirill Varshavskiy. Thank you for the craft, the late nights, and for caring about every detail.

And none of this would have happened without the incredible support of @sumit_c, @elbio_abib, @rroslansky, @clamanna, @jacobandreou and so many others across Microsoft. Thank you for believing in it.

This is just the beginning!

P.S. i made a little film to celebrate. It starts in 1997. Watch till the end.

I never looked at the X algorithm before today. It's open source, and they have a file called param .rs with the actual weights used to rank your “For You feed”

The most surprising thing: copying a post's link has a weight of 20. Liking it has a weight of 0.7. Copying the link is the most valuable thing you can do with a post, weighted almost 30x more than a like and 4x more than a reply.

My guess why: when you copy a link, you're about to paste it somewhere else. A group chat, Slack, an email. That's the strongest signal there is that a post is worth something, and it brings new people onto X. A like costs nothing. Sending something to a friend means you're putting your name on it.

The rest of the list tells a bit of a similar story like a reply is 5, a quote is 5, sharing by DM is 5, following the author is 4, a share is 2.1, a repost is 1, and a like is 0.7. Literally I didn’t know that repost does almost nothing. 

The negatives are brutal btw a report is -234, a mute is -59, "not interested" is -53 and a block is -31.

A reply from someone you follow who follows you back gets a 15x boost. Conversations between real connections matter most (and not bots!)

Reposts don't reach strangers. A filter drops a repost for anyone who doesn't follow the reposter. A quote is a new post, so it can travel much further. Quote beats repost so you always have to add your own thoughts to a post. 

Your post leaves For You after 48 hours. Small accounts get guaranteed test slots while a post is under 2 hours old with fewer than 200 views, so the first 2 hours decide a lot.

Interestingly hashtags aren't read anywhere in the ranking code. They are not a thing anymore. Your text and images are turned into vectors and matched to people with similar interests.

So if you want a post to spread, write something people want to send to one specific person. Likes are nice, but they barely move anything.

No. I'm not saying we are taking this path because we are being compensated for it, or that we are making a trade or a choice based on any kind of reward. Some people may see it that way. I don't. Whether we get some positive things out of this or not changes nothing in this regard. In scenarios where things go exceptionally well and we end up with a benevolent, aligned superintelligence, human disempowerment seems even more likely to me.

Separately, I am against death and work. So against it that it is obviously a scissor for you and me, where it's hard for us to even imagine the other side. But that is a separate issue. 

It's like... okay, imagine two people watching an asteroid enter the atmosphere. One person starts to list all the good things that may happen as a result of the impact. Maybe they think some human systems are so misaligned that only an event like this can change them, or maybe they think the geography in this area is all wrong and that with the mountains gone we'll have far more arable land once things settle down again. Maybe they just owe a lot of money in gambling debts. Their friend disagrees and says, "Are you crazy!? None of that is remotely worth what’s about to happen!"

What I'm trying to say is that the discussion between these two people has nothing to do with gravity.
